newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close down ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close down ahead of report.

text.p: CME pork belly futures fell into the close as local liquidation triggered sell stops and erased earlier gains that had lifted the market to contract highs. Hog futures also eased back to close mixed after showing late strength, traders said.

Pork bellies closed 1.575 cents per lb lower to 0.800 higher with May off the most at 89.825 cents after setting a new high near midday of 92.150 cents. August and February also set new highs and July equaled its old high before falling.
Hog futures ended 0.525 cent lower to 0.375 higher with June off 0.250 at 85.000 cents.

Pork bellies erased early losses that came on profit taking and advanced to new highs on expectations of a bullish out-of-town report. But prices fell in the final few minutes as locals squared positions ahead of the report, traders said.

After the close, the CME reported a net out-movement of 409,000 lbs out of CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago. That compared with analysts' estimates of a net in-movement of 250,000 to 500,000 lbs and pit talk of 200,000 lbs in or less.
"(Belly) futures will be one (cent) to two (cents) higher tomorrow - that market's still bullish," said Dave Maher from Securities Corp of Iowa.

Maher said the industry appeared to be taking bellies out of reporting warehouses and placing them in non-reporting warehouses in preperation for export to Japan. Cash bellies rose to $84 per cwt, the highest level since late September, while the increased storings were taking place, which likely indicates the expected increased exports to Japan.
"I still think the reason the cold storage was higher was due to speculators putting pork away and waiting for the next wave of exports to Japan," Maher said.
Japan announced last week that it was already buying U.S. bellies to meet needs into the end of the year.
Locals pressured May while ABN Chicogo Corp sold July and Rand Financials bought.

Hog futures drifted back to unchanged levels in nearbys and posted net gains in back months late on mixed support before slipping along with pork bellies. An easier tone to cash hogs Tuesday and profit taking from an overbought condition weighed on prices early, traders said.

Packer profit margins are deep in the red and they are cutting back on the rate of hog slaughter as a result. However, overall light hog runs and the expected increased pork exports continued to underpin futures, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index surged $1.49 to $77.74 per cwt.

Lind-Waldock bought June while Rand Financials sold. R.J. O'Brien sold August and locals bought. In hog options, First Chicago bought July 82 puts before the early break in futures. Later, there was general selling of 80 and lower June puts, pit sources said.
